hypothesis: A scalar eight-way unroll may expose more independent minimum/index chains than the previously measured two-, three-, and four-accumulator candidates, reducing loop-carried dependence on random and decreasing inputs. The lower measured aggregate time for two accumulators (2.2604 µs) than for three (3.0152 µs) or four (2.8135 µs) shows that more chains are not automatically better; eight also raises initialization, fold, and instruction-pressure costs, so correctness and per-pattern measurements are needed to assess the tradeoff.
notes: This is a new scalar eight-accumulator candidate; no performance or correctness result is claimed here. The visible historical measurements are aggregate only, so the controller should validate correctness and measure random and decreasing cases before drawing conclusions.
transformations: Added a fixed eight-way scalar scan with eight independent minimum-value and earliest-index accumulators.
Folded the accumulators using signed minimum-value ordering and lowest-index tie-breaking.
Handled n < 8 with a scalar path and processed any trailing elements scalarly after the fold.
Used no explicit SIMD or parallel workers.
